stories.title: Indian Bank opens recruitment for 1500 apprentice posts
stories.summary: Indian Bank has invited applications for 1500 apprentice positions. The registration process is open from November 5 to November 25, 2026. Interested candidates can submit their applications through the bank's official website. The organization is currently seeking to fill these vacancies across its network.

stories.title: SBI opens registration for 77 specialist officer roles
stories.summary: The State Bank of India has opened applications for 77 specialist officer vacancies. The recruitment process is currently underway, with a submission deadline of November 25, 2026. Candidates are directed to the bank's official website to review eligibility requirements and the selection process.

stories.title: SBI seeks 77 specialist officers for fire and security
stories.summary: The State Bank of India is recruiting for 77 specialist officer posts, including 17 fire engineering roles and 60 security management positions. Applications are open until November 25, 2026. The bank has invited eligible candidates to apply through its official portal.

stories.title: TNPSC extends group 4 registration deadline to November 8
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission has extended the application deadline for its Group 4 services to November 8, 2026. The move follows a government decision to increase the maximum age limit by five years for all categories. There are 6,500 vacancies available.

stories.title: TNPSC group 4 application window remains open
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission has extended the registration deadline for the Combined Civil Services Examination IV. The extension follows a five-year increase in the upper age limit for all categories. Candidates can access the official notice and apply through the commission's website.

stories.title: RRB opens applications for 191 isolated category posts
stories.summary: The Railway Recruitment Boards have opened applications for 191 ministerial and isolated category vacancies, including roles for lab assistants and public prosecutors. The registration process closes on December 4, 2026. Interested candidates can apply via the official recruitment portal.

stories.title: HPRCA teacher recruitment notification
stories.summary: The full details regarding the HPRCA recruitment for 2423 PGT teacher posts are currently unavailable due to a server error. Interested applicants should check the official website for updates once the connection is restored.

stories.title: Bank of Baroda seeks 805 managers for wealth services
stories.summary: Bank of Baroda has invited applications for 805 managerial posts within its wealth management services division. The application window closes on November 24, 2026. Interested candidates may review eligibility and selection details on the bank's official website.

stories.title: Supreme Court seeks 130 junior court attendants
stories.summary: The Supreme Court of India is accepting applications for 130 junior court attendant positions. The deadline for submission is November 25, 2026. Eligible candidates are invited to apply through the court's official website.

stories.title: Student wins award for space biology research proposal
stories.summary: Sanskriti Sanvi, a postgraduate student at Chanakya University, has won a 1 lakh rupee national award for her STELLA proposal. The project outlines a multi-stress simulation chamber designed to study microbial responses to space conditions. The award was announced by the Department of Biotechnology.

stories.title: Hydrogen chloride discovery suggests active Martian volcanism
stories.summary: Scientists have detected hydrogen chloride gas above fissures near Alba Mons, suggesting Mars may retain geological activity. The findings, published in Science Advances, challenge the long-held view that the planet's volcanic history is entirely in the past. The interior may be more active than previously assumed.

stories.title: BRAC University hosts AI training camp
stories.summary: BRAC University hosted a two-day workshop for 20 students preparing for the International Artificial Intelligence Olympiad 2027. Organised by the Bangladesh Open Source Network, the event provided specialised training to participants selected from a national competition. The Olympiad aims to foster AI skills among students.

stories.title: CBSE releases 2027 science exam pattern
stories.summary: The CBSE has outlined the 2027 Class 10 science exam structure, featuring an 80-mark theory paper and a 20-mark internal assessment. The three-hour exam includes 39 questions across five sections. The board continues to emphasise competency-based questions as part of its 100-mark evaluation system.

stories.title: Verbal rehearsal as a writing tool
stories.summary: Educators suggest that verbal rehearsal, or thinking out loud, helps students transfer thoughts to the written word. Tanya Baker of the National Writing Project notes the practice is effective for all students, particularly those struggling to start or maintain the writing process. It remains a prewriting and drafting technique.

stories.title: CBSE publishes 2026-27 sample papers
stories.summary: The CBSE has released subject-wise sample papers and marking schemes for the 2026-27 academic session. These materials detail the 80:20 assessment structure, question types, and passing criteria for upcoming board exams. Students are encouraged to use these to understand the structure of the final examinations.

stories.title: Wiregrass Foundation awards fall scholarships
stories.summary: The Wiregrass Georgia Technical College Foundation has awarded fall scholarships to 14 students at its Ben Hill-Irwin Campus. The funding was provided by donors and community supporters to assist students in pursuing their educational goals and preparing for future careers.

stories.title: PM-YASASVI scholarship applications remain open
stories.summary: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is accepting applications for the PM-YASASVI scholarship scheme for OBC, EBC, and DNT students. stories.summary: The I&M Foundation and Moringa School have launched a scholarship program for young Kenyans to pursue software engineering training. stories.summary: The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations is reportedly planning to move the ICSE Class 10 exam start time to 10 AM from 2027. The current start time is 11 AM. The council has not yet published an official timetable to confirm the change.

stories.summary: Kerala Pareeksha Bhavan has released hall tickets for the 2026 Teacher Eligibility Test. The examination is scheduled for 14 November and 15 November, with two shifts held each day. Candidates can download their admit cards through the official state portal.

stories.title: US midterm results and international student policy
stories.summary: Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress in the US midterm elections. While the shift offers a potential counterweight to the administration's immigration agenda, Trump remains in office and continues to oversee visa policy. For international students, the development is currently more sentiment than policy breakthrough.

stories.title: Australia considers tuition deposit requirements for students
stories.summary: The Australian Department of Home Affairs is seeking input on a proposal requiring international students to deposit 50-100 percent of tuition fees into a local bank account before visa application. The plan has sparked controversy over potential financial risks if a student's visa application is eventually rejected.

stories.title: National Overseas Scholarship supports AI studies in Australia
stories.summary: A 26-year-old student from a rural farming family completed a master's degree in Artificial Intelligence at Monash University using the National Overseas Scholarship. The government scheme covered tuition, living expenses and other costs for the student, whose name was changed to protect his privacy during the program.

stories.title: Australia introduces two-year training visa
stories.summary: Australia is offering a subclass 407 training visa allowing foreign nationals to undertake supervised workplace training for up to two years. The program targets individuals seeking professional development or skills for their home country careers, provided they secure an approved sponsor and meet health and character requirements.

stories.title: UK universities report financial strain from visa crackdown
stories.summary: UK universities are facing mounting financial losses as the government's strict visa regime turns away prospective international students. Gillian Murray, vice-chancellor of the University of Bradford, warned that the policy affects all institutions, though some regions are experiencing a more significant impact than others.

stories.title: Germany sees rise in Indian postgraduate students
stories.summary: Germany is becoming a preferred destination for Indian students pursuing technology and computer science degrees. Experts suggest that success in the local job market requires more than a university degree, noting that career planning and German language proficiency remain essential components for students seeking employment after graduation.

stories.title: Democrats take control of US Congress
stories.summary: Democrats have won majorities in both the House and Senate following the US midterm elections. The shift provides an opportunity to challenge immigration proposals affecting international students, though the administration retains control over current visa policies. Immediate relief for students remains unlikely while the current administration stays in office.

stories.title: US midterm results offer optimism for students
stories.summary: Recent US midterm results have provided a sentiment boost for Indian students concerned about immigration restrictions. While experts suggest the shift in Congressional control may help protect against future visa cuts, they note that immediate policy changes are not expected and job market concerns remain for many students.

stories.title: UK universities urge better visa regulation coherence
stories.summary: A report from the Higher Education Policy Institute suggests the UK Home Office and the Office for Students should work more closely to resolve conflicting requirements. The policy note argues that current tensions between the two bodies risk unintended consequences for both international students and higher education institutions.

stories.title: UK to launch refugee student scheme
stories.summary: The UK government is preparing to open applications for a scheme designed to help talented displaced students continue their studies. The initiative follows a pilot program run by Refugee Education UK and aims to provide a safe, legal pathway for students who were previously blocked from education options.

stories.title: Canada denies study permit to Afghan scholarship recipient
stories.summary: A Kabul teenager who secured a full scholarship to a Canadian university prep school was denied a study permit. The Canadian government argued she could not afford tuition, despite the program covering all fees. The student had been banned from classrooms in Afghanistan for four years.

stories.title: Proposed US OPT fees spark discussion
stories.summary: Immigration partners are discussing a proposal that would attach a 70,000 dollar fee to Optional Practical Training, with an additional 30,000 dollar charge for subsequent recommendations. The discussion covers who might bear these costs and the potential impact on current and future participants in the program.

stories.title: NCERT introduces personal finance to Class 9 curriculum
stories.summary: The National Council of Educational Research and Training is adding chapters on personal finance and entrepreneurship to Class 9 Social Science textbooks. Students will learn about mutual funds, taxes, loan repayments and business plans as part of an effort to familiarise them with financial decisions and business operations.

stories.title: Fintech education requires focus beyond technology
stories.summary: India's fintech sector is operating at a massive scale, with UPI processing 23.66 billion transactions in July 2026. Experts argue that universities must prepare students with financial literacy and ethical judgement, as the rapid approval of financial services requires users to understand the products they are using.

stories.title: Microsoft launches AI literacy tools for Filipino teachers
stories.summary: Microsoft has introduced the Elevate for Educators resource suite in the Philippines to help 2,000 teachers earn AI credentials. The program includes classroom toolkits and guides intended to help students think critically about privacy and responsible AI use while providing professional recognition for the participating educators.

stories.title: Robotics education expands across Pakistan
stories.summary: The Pakistan Innovation Quest is working to reach 10,000 learners and 300 teachers through robotics and STEM initiatives. The program aims to remove barriers related to geography, gender and disability by providing a pathway from introductory robotics to regional competitions and a national showcase for students.

stories.title: NIIT University partners with Fractal for AI training
stories.summary: NIIT University and enterprise AI company Fractal are establishing an AI and Analytics Centre of Excellence. The partnership will provide third-year B.Tech students with industry-linked projects, technical guidance and opportunities to work on generative AI, agentic AI and large language model applications through capstone projects.

stories.title: Augusta University develops AI-supported learning tool
stories.summary: Augusta University researchers are developing a software engineering tutor with a 2 million dollar grant from the U.S. National Science Foundation. The tool aims to help students understand why their code fails by providing feedback on security and quality, bridging the gap between identifying errors and applying improvements.

stories.title: Educators in Indonesia seek AI training
stories.summary: Teachers and vocational graduates in Karawang are participating in Microsoft-supported AI training programs to integrate new technology into classrooms. One educator travelled 450 kilometers to attend a session, highlighting the gap between growing interest in AI and the practical skills required to actually use it.

stories.title: Google introduces Guided Learning for classrooms
stories.summary: Google is launching a Guided Learning feature for Search and Classroom designed to act as a personal study partner. The tool avoids providing direct answers, instead guiding students through problems with questions and explanations. It is currently testing in selected US schools before a global rollout.

stories.title: Ghana Education Service completes promotion exercise
stories.summary: More than 60,000 teachers completed a three-day promotion exercise aimed at separating professional ranks from administrative positions. The Ghana Education Service reported a smooth process across all centres. The policy marks a significant shift in how career advancement is structured for the nation's educators.

stories.title: Debate grows over AI in the classroom
stories.summary: As artificial intelligence becomes more capable of performing tasks, educators are questioning the future of human teaching. While AI can answer questions in seconds, proponents argue it cannot replace the human connection required to unlock a child's potential. The definition of human intelligence remains under review.

stories.summary: The Teachers Service Commission has reopened its online performance appraisal portal following weeks of technical failures. Teachers previously struggled with failed logins and disappearing entries. The system is now back online, providing a final window for staff to complete their mandatory submissions.

stories.title: Louisiana Tech receives cybersecurity grant
stories.summary: Louisiana Tech University has secured $612,000 from the U.S. Department of Defense to expand its cybersecurity education programs. The funding includes scholarships for eight students and new training resources for artificial intelligence and security operations. The university aims to strengthen its technical workforce pipeline.

stories.title: Higher education faces AI disruption
stories.summary: The World Economic Forum estimates that 39 percent of existing worker skills will become outdated by 2030 due to AI. Universities are being urged to shift toward lifelong learning and AI literacy to keep graduates relevant. The traditional degree model is now considered a less stable proposition.

stories.title: Teachers share AI classroom experiences
stories.summary: Educators report using AI to develop lesson plans, organize data, and provide feedback on assignments. While some describe the technology as a tool to spark creativity, others remain in search of formal guidance. The impact of these tools is currently being felt across K-12 classrooms.

stories.title: Sindh Education Foundation trains 867 teachers
stories.summary: The Sindh Education Foundation is conducting an eight-day cluster-based training program for 867 teachers in Karachi. The initiative aims to enhance pedagogical skills and promote child-centred teaching practices. Managing Director Gahanwer Ali Laghari visited the centres to observe the training sessions in progress.

stories.title: EAC-PM paper cautions against school mergers
stories.summary: A working paper from the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister recommends that school mergers be used only as a last resort. It calls for 10-year district plans and suggests that institutes share educators and labs to maintain accessibility while rationalising small schools.

stories.title: Karnataka CM urges private schools to adopt government schools, 1,000 institutions to be covered in first phase: Check c
stories.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar has urged private school managements across the state to adopt government schools in rural areas and contribute towards improving their infrastructure and quality of education. Under the state's 'Namma Shaale Namma Javabdari' (Our School, Our Responsibility) programme, the government plans

stories.title: Pathways World School develops AI framework
stories.summary: Pathways World School in Gurgaon has created a structured framework for responsible AI use in classrooms. The school convened a workshop with experts, parents and students to develop governance and literacy policies. The school claims this provides a third path between banning AI and having no guidance.

stories.title: Bihar schools to introduce regional languages
stories.summary: The Bihar government will introduce six regional languages, including Bhojpuri and Maithili, for students in Classes 1 and 2 starting in the 2026-27 academic session. Textbooks are being developed to help children learn in the same language they use at home.

stories.title: Delhi schools increase pollution measures
stories.summary: Delhi schools are planning to postpone outdoor activities, install air purifiers and place snake plants in classrooms as pollution levels rise. The Directorate of Education has directed all schools to organise special assemblies on November 5. The plants have been asked to assist with the air quality.

stories.title: Karnataka government asks private schools to adopt rural counterparts
stories.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar has appealed to private school managements to adopt state-run schools in rural areas. The Namma Shaale Namma Javabdari programme aims to link 1,000 state-run schools with private institutions to improve quality and opportunities. The government is currently looking for volunteers.

stories.title: Australia announces national education overhaul
stories.summary: Australia is launching a sweeping education reform package, including a national digital detox, a revamped maths curriculum and a new commission to oversee testing and teacher standards. Education Minister Jason Clare stated the reforms are designed to support teachers and help children learn.

stories.title: CSIR UGC NET application deadline approaches
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency will close the application process for the CSIR UGC NET December 2026 examination on November 5. Candidates seeking eligibility for Junior Research Fellowship and Assistant Professor positions must submit their forms and fees through the official website by the deadline.

stories.title: Seattle parents request pause on classroom AI
stories.summary: Seattle families are calling for a pause on the district rollout of generative AI tools, citing concerns that technology may harm student learning. Parents are demanding clearer guidance and training before AI tutors and chatbots are integrated further into daily classroom lessons.

stories.title: Google links Search access to AI adoption
stories.summary: Google has announced that schools which restrict AI entirely will lose access to Google Search. Chris Phillips, vice-president for education at Google, stated that search and AI are now deeply integrated. Schools that ban the technology will see a message explaining the loss of access.

stories.title: Independent review ordered into death of Jason Arday
stories.summary: Jason Beer KC will lead an independent review into the death of Cambridge academic Jason Arday. The inquiry will examine the university's handling of misconduct allegations and its support for Arday during his tenure as the institution's youngest black professor.

stories.title: US school choice process remains complex
stories.summary: American parents are navigating a school choice system that includes magnet, charter, virtual and microschools. The process requires creating specific district accounts and entering codes that are case-sensitive. The system offers many options, provided the user can successfully log in.

stories.title: Delhi High Court considers calculator plea
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has issued a notice to the CBSE, NCERT and the central government regarding a petition to allow calculators in Class 12 Accountancy and Maths board exams. The authorities have been given six weeks to respond to the request.

stories.title: Chowgule International School opens admissions
stories.summary: Chowgule International School in Goa has opened admissions for the 2027-28 academic year. The school promotes an inquiry-led learning curriculum focused on critical thinking and holistic development. The institution describes its approach as the secret to future-ready children.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu pushes for medical admission reforms
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has requested that the Nandan Nilekani-led panel abolish the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test. The state government maintains that medical admissions should be based on Class 12 marks rather than entrance examinations.

stories.title: Kerala government questions university appointment
stories.summary: The Kerala Higher Education department has sought an explanation from Calicut University regarding the appointment of P. Rasheed Ahammed as pro-Vice-Chancellor. The department is investigating whether he received proper sanction to leave his previous post at an aided college to take the role.

stories.title: UP relaxes teacher recruitment criteria
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission has revised eligibility rules for the Assistant Teacher recruitment 2026. Candidates who began their teacher education programmes before July 29, 2011, are now exempt from minimum graduation percentage requirements.

stories.title: Indian universities absent from top 50 rankings
stories.summary: No Indian university has featured in the top 50 of the QS Asia Rankings for the second consecutive year. Leading institutions including IIT Delhi and IIT Bombay saw their rankings slip, despite the country increasing its total representation to 325 institutions.

stories.title: IIT Delhi expands mental health services
stories.summary: IIT Delhi will recruit full-time clinical psychologists and counsellors while establishing an independent student grievance ombudsperson. These changes follow recommendations from a committee investigating a recent student death. The institute is also formalising its student re-entry protocols to better support those returning to campus life.
